chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab told us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Maskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both), who said:

The worst of servants is a servant who has two faces and two tongues; he praises his brother in his presence and eats him in his absence. If he is given, he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.

key_terms.ويأكله: and he eats him (idiom for consuming/gossiping)

ai.seo_question: What are the characteristics of the worst type of servant according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), highlighting the spiritual corruption of *al-wajhayn* (two-facedness) as a distinct vice of hypocrisy. The Imam elaborates that such individuals exhibit conditional loyalty, characterized by envy in prosperity and abandonment in adversity, reflecting the inner dissonance between their public persona and private actions. This description serves as a practical ethical guide for Shia believers to identify and avoid the subtle decay of sincerity in social interactions.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ali Majilawayh, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: I was told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hussain bin Abi’l-Khattab, from Hasan bin Ali bin Faddal, from Ali bin Nu’man, from Abdullah, bin Maskan, from Dawud bin Farqad, from Abu Shayba al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja’far, Muhammed bin Ali al-Baqir, peace be upon them both, that he said:

The worst of servants is a servant who has two faces and two tongues; (by which) he is tender with his brother in (his) presence and eats him in (his) absence, (and) if he is given, he envies him, and if he is afflicted, he abandons him.
